findings.text: NEGATIVE_CONTROL_MUTATION is defined and never referenced anywhere in the module, and its value quotes another node's mutation ("Restoring the old first-harness session lookup makes ordinary resume refuse"); the comment above it says it is printed verbatim as the red log's first line, but this node's red logs (negative-control.log, repair-negative-control.log) begin with a '# revision:' header, so the constant is dead code carrying a statement that does not describe any log the node produced. This was raised in the previous review of this node and the repair commit did not touch it.

The receipt branch attributes any growth in launch_failures between the record read at change_lane's entry and the read taken after the spawn to the move just made. A reap or classification pass that appends a launch failure for the previous attempt's worker inside that window (dispatch_launch.py:307 appends from a reaper, dispatch_sessions.py:321 from the classification path) is indistinguishable from a failure of this spawn, so a lane change that did start a worker can be refused and left on the old backend. The docstring's claim that the comparison 'isolates the one this move caused' is stronger than the count comparison can support; matching on the receipt's recorded_at or stream_path against this attempt's log_path would.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the production path is reckon/crew_run_commands.py:2758, the crew resume --backend door, which reaches change_lane through reckon/crew/dispatch.py:468 and reckon/crew/dispatching/_imports.py:710 and emits the returned dict; it does not post-process the pointer itself, so a refused result changes nothing on disk.
item_verdicts.diff: read both commits against ff3bb24bcf: b91a44211d adds _lane_change_launch_failure and _refused_lane_change_result plus the early return and a 381-line test module, and b1bbf77fbebc adds the spawn-liveness and no-stream branch with a second-attempt test; nothing outside the two expected paths changed.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_refused_lane_change_leaves_the_pointer.py covering an accepted launch with no worker, a move refused before launch, a move whose worker starts, and the lane-change record written only in the last case; all four cases exist in the module and the manifest records the run at b1bbf77f as 62 passed, EXIT=0 in after-suite.log.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that a lane change whose launch starts no worker leaves the run pointer's backend, attempt, agent and dialect unchanged and returns a result naming why; reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1809 reads the pointer after the spawn and reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:2215 returns _refused_lane_change_result instead of committing the move.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the reviewed run's manifest.md: it reports status complete, the two commits b91a44211d and b1bbf77fbebc, a baseline arm of 58 passed at ff3bb24bcf, an after arm of 62 passed at b1bbf77f, and a repair negative control failing at the pre-repair head; the logs it cites carry those figures and a bare EXIT line.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the node declared four paths; the delivered diff touches exactly reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py and tests/test_a_refused_lane_change_leaves_the_pointer.py, both declared, and the two docs paths (fragment and figures) carry nothing in this diff.

justifications.durability: the declared negative control is real (negative-control.log fails the accepted-launch case at ff3bb24bcf with the backend moved) and the repair's own control (repair-negative-control.log) fails the second-attempt case at b91a44211d, so both landed branches redden on reinstating the regression; the phase-transition branch at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1844 is the one path no test distinguishes, and it is redundant today because every writer that sets LAUNCH_FAILED_PHASE also appends a receipt (dispatch_launch.py:364, dispatch_sessions.py:323).
justifications.evidence: baseline-suite.log (58 passed at ff3bb24bcf) and after-suite.log (62 passed at b1bbf77f) each open with revision, tree, cwd, command and module.__file__ and end in a bare EXIT=0, and the two red logs record the failures that justify the guard, so the manifest's figures reconcile with the logs it names.
justifications.fit: the two helpers at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1809 follow the module's mechanism-named, docstringed style with no plan or ticket identifier, but tests/test_a_refused_lane_change_leaves_the_pointer.py:43 still carries a dead constant quoting another node's mutation beside a comment that misdescribes the red log's first line.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1848 asks the launch path's own no-worker question (process gone, stream never begun) beside the receipt and phase checks, so a second lane change on a run already in the launch-failed phase is refused too and the four fields stay on the source attempt; the move still commits when the worker starts, as tests/test_a_refused_lane_change_leaves_the_pointer.py:359 asserts.
justifications.reuse: the guard reads the owner's existing facts rather than adding a parallel notion of a failed start: _stream_began is imported from reckon/crew/dispatch_launch.py:1914, and LAUNCH_FAILED_PHASE, process_alive and the launch_failures receipt are reused, though the no-worker question is re-derived at reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py:1848 rather than exposed by the launch path's own _record_launch_failure.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the delivered diff (reckon/crew/dispatch_sessions.py and tests/test_a_refused_lane_change_leaves_the_pointer.py) is inside the node's declared write paths and carries nothing the goal does not imply; the docs fragment and figure paths the node declared are simply absent.
